docs.title: BioPal SpectraUV Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the BioPal SpectraUV system documentation! This site provides comprehensive guides for operators, system administrators, and developers working with the spectroscopy data acquisition and publication platform.

docs.title: What is SpectraUV?
docs.text:
SpectraUV is a Python-based system that:

  • Acquires UV-Vis spectral data from binary spectrum files
  • Parses spectral absorption values across the UV range (190-391 nm)
  • Publishes data via OPC UA for integration with industrial SCADA systems
  • Manages data persistence through Redis for inter-process communication

The system is designed for high-performance, real-time spectroscopy measurement workflows in industrial environments.

docs.title: Spectral Parser (parsing_spectra.py)
docs.text: Parses binary .bin files containing UV-Vis absorption spectra. Validates file integrity and extracts 201 floating-point absorption values.

docs.title: OPC UA Server (opcua_server.py)
docs.text: Exposes parsed spectral data as OPC UA variables for real-time access by SCADA systems and industrial clients. Supports two spectrometer channels with five data types each.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • Redis server (for inter-process communication)
  • OPC UA client (to consume published data)
  • Linux or Windows with .NET support (for full system)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: SpectraUV is a distributed system for acquiring and publishing UV-Vis spectral data in real-time. The architecture centers around Redis as a message bus, enabling decoupled, scalable inter-process communication.

docs.title: 1. Spectral Data Acquisition
docs.text:
• Binary spectral files (.bin) are retrieved from FTP or local storage
  • parsing_spectra.parsebinary() parses the binary format:
  • Validates magic byte markers (0xEFBEADDE)
  • Extracts 201 floating-point absorption values
  • Returns tuple spanning wavelengths 190-391 nm (1 nm steps)
  • Parsed data is stored in Redis with keys like transmission_channel_1

docs.title: 2. Data Publication (OPC UA)
docs.text:
• opcua_server.opcua_loop() runs an async loop every 1 second
  • Polls Redis for updates to spectral data keys
  • Updates OPC UA server variables with latest absorption values
  • SCADA systems and industrial clients subscribe to these variables

docs.title: 3. Inter-Process Communication
docs.text:
• Redis serves as the central hub for state management
  • Processes communicate asynchronously without tight coupling
  • Enables horizontal scaling (add new readers/writers without modifying existing code)

docs.title: Input: Binary Spectrum File (.bin)
docs.text:
Bytes     Content
─────────────────────────────────
0-3       Magic marker: 0xEFBEADDE
4-79      Metadata (file header info)
80-...    Spectral data (float32 values, little-endian)
          Total: 201 values × 4 bytes = 804 bytes
...       (content)
-4-(-1)   Magic marker: 0xEFBEADDE

Wavelength mapping: Each float value corresponds to 1 nm steps starting at 190 nm - Value[0] → 190 nm - Value[1] → 191 nm - ... - Value[200] → 390 nm

docs.title: Output: OPC UA Variables
docs.text: Each spectrometer channel exposes: - transmission — Raw transmission spectrum (201 floats) - absorbance — Calculated absorbance (A = -log10(transmission)) - onlinereference — Reference spectrum from latest calibration - sample — Active sample measurement - calibration — Calibration data used for normalization - wavelengths — Wavelength axis (190.0 to 390.0 nm, read-only)

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text: Component Technology Purpose Message Bus Redis State storage, inter-process communication Spectral Parsing Python struct module Binary data deserialization OPC UA Server asyncua (1.1.8+) Industrial protocol for SCADA integration Async Runtime asyncio Concurrent I/O operations Process Communication JSON over Redis Serialize complex data types

docs.title: Scalability Considerations
docs.text:
• Single-threaded Python with asyncio handles concurrent operations efficiently
  • Redis can scale horizontally with Redis Cluster for distributed deployments
  • OPC UA clients can connect independently; server scales with client connections
  • Each component (parser, OPC server) can run on separate machines sharing Redis

docs.title: Environment Configuration
docs.text:
Key environment variables:

REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=10.20.20.11          # Redis host
REDIS_PORT_NUMBER=6379                 # Redis port
OPC_IP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0                 # OPC UA listen address
OPC_PORT_NUMBER=4841                   # OPC UA port (standard)

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• OPC UA server runs without authentication by default
  • Redis access is unauthenticated by default
  • For production: Use firewall rules, VPN, or configure Redis password authentication
  • Binary file validation uses magic bytes, not cryptographic signatures

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide covers common tasks and workflows for operating and extending the SpectraUV system.

docs.title: Binary Spectrum File Format
docs.text: SpectraUV expects binary files in a specific format. Understanding this format is critical for troubleshooting and data validation.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
Offset    Size    Description
────────────────────────────────────────
0         4       Magic Marker: 0xEFBEADDE
4         76      Metadata (header info, not currently parsed)
80        804     Spectral Data (201 × float32, little-endian)
884       4       Magic Marker: 0xEFBEADDE

Total:    888 bytes

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The parsebinary() function validates file integrity by checking:

  1. Start marker (bytes 0-3): Must equal 0xEFBEADDE
  2. End marker (bytes 884-887): Must equal 0xEFBEADDE
  3. Data length: Exactly 804 bytes (201 × 4 bytes per float)

If markers are missing or incorrect, parsing raises ValueError: Bad file markers.

docs.title: Wavelength Mapping
docs.text:
Spectral values are indexed by wavelength position:

wavelength_nm = 190 + index

spectrum[0]   # 190 nm
spectrum[100] # 290 nm
spectrum[200] # 390 nm

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse a spectrum file
spectrum = parsebinary('/path/to/spectrum.bin')

# spectrum is a tuple of 201 floats
print(f"Parsed {len(spectrum)} wavelength points")
print(f"190 nm: {spectrum[0]:.4f}")
print(f"390 nm: {spectrum[200]:.4f}")

docs.title: Storing in Redis
docs.text:
import json
import redis
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse and store
spectrum = parsebinary('/path/to/spectrum.bin')
r = redis.Redis(host='localhost', decode_responses=True)

# Convert tuple to list for JSON serialization
r.set('transmission_channel_1', json.dumps(list(spectrum)))

# Verify storage
stored = json.loads(r.get('transmission_channel_1'))
print(f"Stored {len(stored)} values in Redis")

docs.title: Advanced: Processing Multiple Spectra
docs.text:
import os
import json
import redis
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

spectrum_dir = '/path/to/spectrum/files'
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

for filename in os.listdir(spectrum_dir):
    if not filename.endswith('.bin'):
        continue

    try:
        spectrum = parsebinary(os.path.join(spectrum_dir, filename))

        # Create Redis key based on filename and channel
        key = f"transmission_channel_1_{filename}"
        r.set(key, json.dumps(list(spectrum)))

        print(f"✓ Stored {filename}")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"✗ Failed {filename}: {e}")

docs.title: How OPC UA Publishing Works
docs.text:
1. OPC UA Server starts and creates two channel objects (spectrouv_1, spectrouv_2)
  2. Server polling loop runs every 1 second:
  3. Scans Redis for keys matching {datatype}* (e.g., transmission*)
  4. Parses JSON values from Redis
  5. Updates corresponding OPC UA node variables
  6. OPC UA clients receive notifications when values change

docs.title: Monitoring Published Data
docs.text:
Check which data types are available in Redis:

import redis

r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

datatypes = ['transmission', 'absorbance', 'onlinereference', 'sample', 'calibration']

for dtype in datatypes:
    keys = list(r.scan_iter(f"{dtype}*"))
    print(f"{dtype}: {keys}")

# Example output:
# transmission: ['transmission_channel_1', 'transmission_channel_2']
# absorbance: ['absorbance_channel_1']
# ...

docs.title: Connecting OPC UA Clients
docs.text:
Popular OPC UA clients:

  • UaExpert (Unified Automation) — Windows GUI client
  • Python asyncua library — Programmatic access
  • Kepware — Enterprise gateway
  • Any standards-compliant OPC UA client

Example Python client:

import asyncio
from asyncua import Client

async def main():
    client = Client("opc.tcp://localhost:4841")
    async with client:
        # Get transmission spectrum for channel 1
        node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=transmission_channel_1")
        value = await node.read_value()
        print(f"Channel 1 Transmission: {value[:5]}...")  # First 5 values

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Spectrum File Not Parsing
docs.text:
Symptom: ValueError: Bad file markers

Causes: - File is corrupted or incomplete - File is not in SpectraUV binary format - File was truncated during transfer

Solution: 1. Verify file size: Should be exactly 888 bytes 2. Check file magic bytes: 

hexdump -C spectrum.bin | head -1  # Should show: ef be ad de
3. Re-download or regenerate the file from the spectrometer

docs.title: OPC UA Variables Not Updating
docs.text:
Symptom: Connected to OPC UA server but variables show all zeros or don't change

Causes: - No spectral data in Redis - Redis not accessible from OPC UA server - Channel names don't match (e.g., using channel_1 but storing as ch1)

Solution: 1. Check Redis has data: 

import redis
r = redis.Redis()
print(r.keys("*"))  # List all keys
2. Verify Redis connection in OPC UA server logs 3. Ensure keys follow exact naming: {datatype}_channel_{1|2}

docs.title: High CPU Usage
docs.text:
Symptom: OPC UA server process using 100% CPU

Causes: - Polling loop waiting for Redis connection - Network latency causing retry loops - Python asyncio event loop spinning

Solution: - Check Redis connectivity - Monitor network latency - Review logs for connection errors

docs.title: Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• Polling interval: Currently 1 second; adjustable in opcua_server.py:106
  • Spectral data size: 201 values × 4 bytes = 804 bytes per spectrum
  • Throughput: Up to 1 spectrum/second with default 1s polling
  • Clients: Server handles 10+ simultaneous OPC UA client connections

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get the SpectraUV system running in 5 minutes!

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+ with pip
  • Redis running on localhost:6379 (or configured via REDIS_IP_ADDRESS)
  • Binary spectrum file (.bin) for testing

docs.title: Step 1: Install Dependencies (2 min)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Sir-Narwhal/biopat-spectrouv-server-1.git
cd biopat-spectrouv-server-1

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # or: venv\Scripts\activate (Windows)

pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Step 2: Start Redis (1 min)
docs.text:
# Option A: Docker (recommended)
docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:latest

# Option B: Native Redis (if installed)
redis-server --port 6379

Verify Redis is running: 

redis-cli ping
# Expected: PONG

docs.title: Step 3: Start OPC UA Server (1 min)
docs.text:
In a new terminal:

cd /path/to/biopat-spectrouv-server-1
source venv/bin/activate  # or: venv\Scripts\activate (Windows)

python parselibrary/opcua_server.py

Expected output: 

6
[OPC UA] Server Started

The OPC UA server is now running on opc.tcp://localhost:4841 and reading from Redis.

docs.title: Step 4: Parse Spectral Data (1 min)
docs.text:
In another terminal:

cd /path/to/biopat-spectrouv-server-1
source venv/bin/activate

python -c "
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary
import json
import redis

# Parse a spectrum (update path to your .bin file)
spectrum = parsebinary('/path/to/your/spectrum.bin')

# Store in Redis
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)
r.set('transmission_channel_1', json.dumps(list(spectrum)))

print(f'Stored {len(spectrum)} wavelength points in Redis')
print(f'Range: {spectrum[0]:.4f} to {spectrum[-1]:.4f}')
"

docs.title: Step 5: Connect OPC UA Client
docs.text:
Connect any OPC UA client to opc.tcp://localhost:4841 and you should see:

Root
├── spectrouv_1
│   ├── transmission_channel_1 (transmission spectrum, 201 values)
│   ├── absorbance_channel_1
│   ├── onlinereference_channel_1
│   ├── sample_channel_1
│   ├── calibration_channel_1
│   └── Wavelength (190-391 nm, 201 values)
└── spectrouv_2
    ├── transmission_channel_2
    ├── absorbance_channel_2
    ├── onlinereference_channel_2
    ├── sample_channel_2
    ├── calibration_channel_2
    └── Wavelength

docs.title: Verification Checklist
docs.text:
• Redis server is running (redis-cli ping returns PONG)
  • OPC UA server started without errors and shows "Server Started"
  • Spectrum file was parsed and stored in Redis
  • OPC UA client connected successfully
  • OPC UA variables are visible and update every second

docs.title: OPC UA server won't start
docs.text:
Connection refused: No address associated with hostname

Check Redis is accessible: 

redis-cli -h localhost ping

docs.title: Spectrum parse fails
docs.text:
ValueError: Bad file markers

Ensure your .bin file is valid (starts and ends with magic bytes 0xEFBEADDE).

docs.title: OPC UA client can't connect
docs.text:
• Check firewall rules on port 4841
  • Verify server is running: ps aux | grep opcua_server.py
  • Check network connectivity to server host

Create a .env file in the project root or set environment variables:

# OPC UA configuration

docs.text: No additional config files are required. All settings are environment variable-based for flexibility in containerized deployments.

Solution: Ensure Redis is running and accessible on the configured host/port

Solution: Use higher port number (> 1024) or run with elevated privileges. Default port 4841 may be restricted on some systems.

python parselibrary/opcua_server.py

docs.title: Error: Connection refused
docs.text:
redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to localhost:6379

Diagnosis: 

# Check if Redis is running
redis-cli ping
# If nothing: Redis is not running

# Check if port 6379 is listening
netstat -an | grep 6379
lsof -i :6379  (macOS/Linux)
netstat -ano | findstr :6379  (Windows)

Solutions:

  1. Start Redis 

    # Docker (recommended)
docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:latest

# Or native Redis
redis-server --port 6379

  2. Verify from Python 

    import redis
r = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379)
print(r.ping())  # Should print: True

  3. Check firewall rules (remote Redis) 

    # Test connectivity
nc -zv <REDIS_IP> 6379
telnet <REDIS_IP> 6379

docs.title: Error: ValueError: Bad file markers
docs.text:
What it means: The binary file doesn't have the correct magic bytes (0xEFBEADDE).

Diagnosis: 

# Check file size (should be exactly 888 bytes)
wc -c spectrum.bin
ls -l spectrum.bin

# Check magic bytes
hexdump -C spectrum.bin | head -1
hexdump -C spectrum.bin | tail -1
# Both should show: ef be ad de

Solutions:

  1. File is corrupted — Re-download or regenerate from spectrometer
  2. Wrong file format — Ensure file comes from SpectraUV spectrometer, not generic binary

  3. Partial file transfer — File transfer was incomplete 

    # Check if file size is 888
if [ $(stat -f%z spectrum.bin) -eq 888 ]; then echo "Size OK"; fi

  4. Byte order issue — If you created the file programmatically, verify: 

    # Correct (little-endian float32)
struct.pack('<f', 0.123)

# Wrong (big-endian)
struct.pack('>f', 0.123)

docs.title: Error: Permission denied on port 4841
docs.text:
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied

Solutions:

  1. Use a port > 1024 (doesn't require root/admin) 

    export OPC_PORT_NUMBER=8841
python parselibrary/opcua_server.py

  2. Run with elevated privileges 

    # Linux/macOS
sudo python parselibrary/opcua_server.py

# Windows (Run as Administrator)
python parselibrary/opcua_server.py

  3. Check if port is in use 

    lsof -i :4841         # macOS/Linux
netstat -ano | findstr :4841  # Windows

# Kill process using port
kill -9 <PID>         # macOS/Linux
taskkill /PID <PID> /F  # Windows

docs.title: Error: Server starts but OPC UA clients can't connect
docs.text:
opc.tcp://localhost:4841 — Connection refused

Solutions:

  1. Verify server is listening 

    netstat -an | grep LISTEN | grep 4841

  2. Check network connectivity 

    ping localhost
nc -zv localhost 4841

  3. Try connecting from another machine 

    # From remote machine, try:
nc -zv <server_ip> 4841

  4. Firewall is blocking port 

    # Linux: Check iptables
iptables -L | grep 4841

# Windows: Check Windows Firewall
# Settings → Security → Firewall → Allow app through firewall

docs.title: Error: OPC UA variables show all zeros
docs.text:
Diagnosis:

  1. Check Redis has data 

    import redis
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

# Should return a list of keys
keys = r.keys('*')
print(keys)

# Check specific datatype
transmission_keys = r.keys('transmission*')
print(transmission_keys)

  2. Verify data is valid JSON 

    import redis, json
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

data = r.get('transmission_channel_1')
if data:
    parsed = json.loads(data)
    print(f"Values: {parsed[:5]}...")  # First 5 values

Solutions:

  1. Store test data in Redis 

    import redis, json
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

# Store dummy spectrum
dummy = [0.5] * 201  # 201 values
r.set('transmission_channel_1', json.dumps(dummy))
r.set('transmission_channel_2', json.dumps(dummy))

  2. Verify OPC UA server is reading Redis

  3. Check logs for "scan_iter" operations

  4. Monitor Redis calls: redis-cli --monitor

  5. Check channel naming

  6. Must be exactly: {datatype}_channel_{1|2}
  7. Not: datatype_ch_1, datatype_ch1, etc.

docs.title: Error: struct.error: unpack requires a buffer of X bytes
docs.text:
struct.error: unpack requires a buffer of 804 bytes

Meaning: Binary file is truncated or has fewer spectral values than expected.

Solutions:

  1. Check file size 

    # Must be exactly 888 bytes total
# 4 (start marker) + 76 (metadata) + 804 (data) + 4 (end marker)
wc -c spectrum.bin

  2. Verify file completeness 

    import struct

with open('spectrum.bin', 'rb') as f:
    raw = f.read()

print(f"Total bytes: {len(raw)}")
print(f"Start marker valid: {raw[:4] == b'\\xef\\xbe\\xad\\xde'}")
print(f"End marker valid: {raw[-4:] == b'\\xef\\xbe\\xad\\xde'}")
print(f"Data section size: {len(raw[80:-4])} (should be 804)")

docs.title: High CPU Usage
docs.text:
Diagnosis: 

# Monitor process
top -p <PID>    # macOS/Linux
# Or use Task Manager (Windows)

# Check if stuck in loop
strace -p <PID> # Linux
dtrace -p <PID> # macOS (requires sudo)

Common causes:

  1. Redis not accessible — Server stuck retrying connection 

    # Check logs for connection errors
# Verify Redis is running and accessible

  2. asyncio event loop spinning — Check for exceptions in try/except blocks 

    # Look for: logger.warning() calls in opcua_loop

  3. Many OPC UA clients — Disconnect idle clients

docs.title: Memory Leak
docs.text:
Monitor memory usage: 

import psutil
import time

p = psutil.Process()
for _ in range(10):
    mem = p.memory_info().rss / 1024 / 1024  # MB
    print(f"{mem:.1f} MB")
    time.sleep(5)

Common causes:

  1. Large spectral arrays not garbage collected
  2. Redis connection pool growing unbounded
  3. Asyncio tasks not properly cleaned up

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.opcua_server
docs.text: This module implements an OPC UA server that publishes UV-Vis spectral data for real-time access by industrial control systems and SCADA platforms.

docs.title: Function: opcua_loop()
docs.text: async def opcua_loop(redis_server: redis.Redis) -> None:

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Run the OPC UA server and continuously publish spectral data from Redis to connected SCADA clients.

Creates an OPC UA server with a BioPal SpectraUV namespace containing two spectrometer channels (spectrouv_1, spectrouv_2). Each channel exposes five spectral data types (transmission, absorbance, reference, sample, calibration) plus a wavelength axis. The server polls Redis every 1 second for updated spectral values and pushes them to OPC UA clients, enabling real-time subscription and monitoring.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: redis_server: redis.Redis - An active Redis connection (authenticated and validated) - Port: 6379 (default) or as configured - Must have decode_responses=True for string operations - Example: redis.Redis(host="localhost", port=6379, decode_responses=True)

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: None - Function runs indefinitely until process termination - Blocks the calling coroutine

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The function executes an infinite async loop with these steps:

  1. Initialization (runs once)
  2. Creates OPC UA Server instance
  3. Registers BioPal SpectraUV namespace
  4. Creates two channel objects (spectrouv_1, spectrouv_2)
  5. For each channel and datatype, creates writable OPC UA variables

  6. Creates read-only wavelength axis variable (190-391 nm)

  7. Polling Loop (repeats every 1 second)

  8. Scans Redis for keys matching patterns: transmission*, absorbance*, etc.
  9. For each key found:
    • Retrieves JSON-encoded spectral data from Redis
    • Identifies target channel (channel_1 or channel_2)
    • Updates corresponding OPC UA variable with new values
  10. Sleeps 1 second before next poll
  11. Catches and logs exceptions (continues operating if errors occur)

docs.title: OPC UA Namespace Structure
docs.text:
ns=1 (BioPal SpectraUV)
├── spectrouv_1 (Object)
│   ├── transmission_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── absorbance_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── onlinereference_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── sample_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── calibration_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   └── Wavelength (Variable, 201 floats, read-only)
└── spectrouv_2 (Object)
    ├── transmission_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── absorbance_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── onlinereference_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── sample_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── calibration_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    └── Wavelength (Variable, 201 floats, read-only)

docs.title: Data Type Definitions
docs.text:
Each datatype variable contains 201 floating-point values:

Datatype Meaning Source transmission Raw transmission spectrum (I/I₀) Direct measurement absorbance Calculated absorbance (A = -log₁₀T) Derived from transmission onlinereference Reference/calibration spectrum Stored calibration sample Active sample measurement Current measurement calibration Calibration data used Reference baseline

docs.title: Wavelength Axis
docs.text:
• 201 values from 190.0 to 390.0 nm
  • Spacing: 1.0 nm between consecutive values
  • Read-only: Cannot be modified via OPC UA clients

docs.title: Redis Key Naming Convention
docs.text:
The server scans Redis for keys following this pattern:

{datatype}_{channel}

Examples:
transmission_channel_1
absorbance_channel_2
onlinereference_channel_1

Valid pattern components:

Component Valid Values {datatype} transmission, absorbance, onlinereference, sample, calibration {channel} channel_1, channel_2

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration is via environment variables:

REDIS_IP_ADDRESS = os.environ.get("REDIS_IP_ADDRESS", "10.20.20.11")
REDIS_PORT_NUMBER = int(os.environ.get("REDIS_PORT_NUMBER", 6379))
OPC_IP_ADDRESS = os.environ.get("OPC_IP_ADDRESS", "0.0.0.0")
OPC_PORT_NUMBER = int(os.environ.get("OPC_PORT_NUMBER", 4841))
Variable Default Purpose REDIS_IP_ADDRESS 10.20.20.11 Redis host IP REDIS_PORT_NUMBER 6379 Redis port OPC_IP_ADDRESS 0.0.0.0 OPC UA listen address (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces) OPC_PORT_NUMBER 4841 OPC UA port (standard)

docs.title: Exceptions & Error Handling
docs.text:
The function catches and logs exceptions internally, allowing the server to continue operating even if errors occur:

Common exceptions:

Exception Cause Recovery redis.ConnectionError Redis unavailable Retries next poll json.JSONDecodeError Invalid JSON in Redis Logs warning, skips key KeyError Channel not recognized Logs warning, skips value Exception General error Logged, server continues

All exceptions are logged via Python logging at WARNING level.

docs.title: Basic Startup
docs.text:
import redis
import asyncio
from parselibrary.opcua_server import opcua_loop

async def main():
    # Connect to Redis
    r = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379, decode_responses=True)

    # Run OPC UA server
    await opcua_loop(r)

# Run forever
asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Command-line Execution
docs.text:
# With environment variables
export REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=192.168.1.10
export OPC_PORT_NUMBER=8841
python -m parselibrary.opcua_server

docs.text:
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY parselibrary/ parselibrary/
ENV REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=redis
ENV OPC_IP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
CMD ["python", "-m", "parselibrary.opcua_server"]

docs.title: Publishing Data to Redis
docs.text:
import json
import redis
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse spectrum
spectrum = parsebinary("/data/sample.bin")

# Connect to Redis
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

# Publish to Redis for OPC UA server to read
r.set("transmission_channel_1", json.dumps(list(spectrum)))

# Server will pick this up in next polling cycle (~1 second)
print("Spectrum published")

docs.title: Connecting OPC UA Client
docs.text:
import asyncio
from asyncua import Client

async def connect():
    client = Client("opc.tcp://localhost:4841")
    async with client:
        # Browse namespace
        root = client.get_root_node()
        objects = await root.get_children()

        # Get transmission data for channel 1
        node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=transmission_channel_1")
        value = await node.read_value()

        print(f"Got {len(value)} wavelength points")
        print(f"First 5 values: {value[:5]}")

        # Subscribe to changes
        async def on_change(node, var):
            print(f"Value changed: {var}")

        handler = await node.subscribe_value(on_change)

        # Keep connection open
        await asyncio.sleep(10)

asyncio.run(connect())

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text:
• Polling latency: ~1 second (configurable in source code, line 106)
  • OPC UA update frequency: 1 Hz
  • Redis scan time: ~5-50 ms per poll (depends on key count)
  • Memory overhead: ~5 MB for 2 channels × 5 datatypes × 201 values
  • Max concurrent clients: 10-50 (asyncio limited)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Events are logged at level WARNING (configured in source):

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)

Change level for more verbose output:

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.parsing_spectra
docs.text: This module provides functions for parsing binary UV-Vis spectral data files.

docs.title: Function: parsebinary()
docs.text: def parsebinary(binfile: str) -> Tuple[float, ...]:

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Parse a binary spectral data file (.bin) and extract absorption values.

Reads a binary file containing UV-Vis spectral data with magic byte markers, validates file integrity, skips metadata, and extracts floating-point absorption values for wavelengths in the UV range (190-391 nm).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: binfile: str - Absolute path to the binary .bin file to parse - Example: "/data/spectra/spectrum_001.bin"

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Tuple[float, ...] - Tuple of 201 floating-point numbers representing absorption values - Index maps to wavelength: wavelength_nm = 190 + index - Values are unitless absorption coefficients (typically 0.0 to 2.5)

docs.title: Raises
docs.text:
ValueError - Raised if file does not have correct magic byte markers (0xEFBEADDE) at start and end - Indicates corrupted, incomplete, or incorrect file format - Message: "Bad file markers"

FileNotFoundError - Raised if the specified file does not exist

IOError - Raised if file cannot be read due to permissions or I/O errors

docs.title: File Format Requirements
docs.text:
Input file must follow exact binary format:

Byte Range    Size    Content
────────────────────────────────────
0-3           4       Magic marker: 0xEFBEADDE
4-79          76      Metadata (file header, not parsed)
80-883        804     Spectral data (201 × 4-byte float32, little-endian)
884-887       4       Magic marker: 0xEFBEADDE

Total:        888 bytes

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse a spectrum file
spectrum = parsebinary("/data/sample_001.bin")

# Access wavelength data
print(f"190 nm: {spectrum[0]:.4f}")     # First value
print(f"290 nm: {spectrum[100]:.4f}")   # Middle value
print(f"390 nm: {spectrum[200]:.4f}")   # Last value

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

try:
    spectrum = parsebinary("/data/corrupted.bin")
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("File not found")
except ValueError as e:
    print(f"Invalid spectrum file: {e}")

docs.title: Processing Multiple Files
docs.text:
import os
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

spectrum_dir = "/data/spectra"
spectra = {}

for filename in os.listdir(spectrum_dir):
    if not filename.endswith('.bin'):
        continue

    try:
        path = os.path.join(spectrum_dir, filename)
        spectrum = parsebinary(path)
        spectra[filename] = spectrum
        print(f"✓ Loaded {filename}")
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
        print(f"✗ Failed {filename}: {e}")

print(f"Loaded {len(spectra)} spectra")

docs.title: Integration with OPC UA
docs.text:
import json
import redis
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse and publish to Redis for OPC UA server
spectrum = parsebinary("/data/sample.bin")

# Store as JSON for Redis
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)
r.set("transmission_channel_1", json.dumps(list(spectrum)))

# OPC UA server will read this and publish via OPC UA
print("Spectrum published to Redis")

docs.title: Performance Notes
docs.text:
• Parsing time: ~1-5 ms per file (single-threaded)
  • Memory usage: ~2 KB per spectrum tuple (201 floats)
  • Throughput: Can parse ~100-200 files/second with asyncio

docs.title: Wavelength Mapping
docs.text:
The returned tuple maps directly to wavelengths:

Index Wavelength (nm) 0 190 1 191 ... ... 100 290 ... ... 200 390

docs.title: Data Type Details
docs.text:
• Values: Single-precision floating-point (32-bit)
  • Byte order: Little-endian (standard Intel/x86)
  • Range: Typically 0.0 to 2.5 (absorption coefficient)
  • Precision: ~6 significant decimal digits
